edits.old: WiredTiger timestamps express application time, separate from internal transaction IDs. They are unsigned 64-bit values; API configuration strings encode them in hexadecimal without a leading 0x. (high confidence)
edits.new: WiredTiger timestamps express application time and operate in parallel with WiredTiger's internal transaction ID management. Applications represent them as unsigned 64-bit integral values; the API passes them as hexadecimal-encoded strings (for example, oldest_timestamp=2a). Sources: https://source.wiredtiger.com/mongodb-5.0/transactions.html ; https://source.wiredtiger.com/develop/struct_w_t___c_o_n_n_e_c_t_i_o_n.html

statements.statement: WiredTiger timestamps express application time, separate from internal transaction IDs.
statements.note: Applications supply their own notion of time; the mechanism runs in parallel with transaction IDs.

statements.statement: API configuration strings encode timestamps in hexadecimal without a leading 0x.
statements.note: Hex encoding is documented, and the examples (2a) have no 0x prefix. No explicit no-0x rule was found, so the correction states hex and gives the example.

edits.rationale: The 5.0 transactions page supports the unsigned 64-bit and parallel-to-transaction-ID points. The WT_CONNECTION API reference shows timestamps encoded as hexadecimal strings, with examples like oldest_timestamp=2a. No page states a rule about a leading 0x; the examples only show it absent, so that part is not stated as a rule.

edits.old: Failing to advance oldest and stable as writes accumulate can retain history and increase cache pressure. Alibaba Cloud's MongoDB 4.0 explanation independently emphasizes timely advancement of both boundaries. (high confidence)
edits.new: Failing to advance oldest and stable as writes accumulate can retain history and increase cache pressure: applications must move both timestamps forward relative to the amount of data being written. Sources: https://source.wiredtiger.com/mongodb-6.0/timestamp_global_api.html

evidence.quote: Applications must move both timestamps forward relative to the amount of data being written; not updating them can result in pinning large amounts of data in the cache, which can in turn affect application performance.
